title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is p.1 of a typed letter from Grothendieck to Lipman Bers, dated Les Aumettes, 15.4.1984. It sets up a problem from the Grothendieck–Ladegaillerie microseminar on Teichmüller spaces and groups.

(1) Reference surface. Fix a compact oriented surface X_0 of genus g with ν boundary components ('holes'), with 2g-2+ν>0 (hyperbolic type).

(2) The 'algebraic' Teichmüller space. T_{g,ν} = \tilde M_{g,ν} classifies smooth complex projective curves X of genus g with ν distinct marked points S. Each comes with a 'Teichmüller rigidification', i.e. a marking X_0 ≃ X∖S. T_{g,ν} is homeomorphic to C^d with d=3g-3+ν. It is the universal cover, in the orbifold/stack sense, of the Deligne–Mumford moduli stack M_{g,ν}, which is the object Grothendieck says he really cares about.

(3) Thurston's bordered Teichmüller space. Thurston instead uses compact bordered Riemann surfaces. Each carries a canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary (uniformize the Schottky double). This gives \tilde{MB}_{g,ν} ≅ C^d × (R_{>0})^ν. The extra ν real parameters are the hyperbolic lengths l_i of the boundary curves. The real dimension count 6g-6+3ν = 2d+ν is correct, e.g. via Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates.

(4) The problem. Determine the precise relation between the two spaces. The idea is to view a punctured curve as the limit of bordered surfaces as all l_i→0. So both spaces should sit inside a third space, of surfaces with 'generalized boundary', where some boundary components may degenerate to a point (cusps / marked points).

The next page continues the construction:
- this space is ≅ C^d × (R_{≥0})^ν, a topological manifold with boundary (with corners in the real-analytic sense), with T_{g,ν} as the deepest corner stratum (all l_i=0);
- Grothendieck asks for an intrinsic, Mod-equivariant (R_{≥0})^ν semigroup action. Its free (R_{>0})^ν part acts on the interior, with quotient T_{g,ν}, and the λ=0 element gives a retraction onto T_{g,ν};
- he notes that 'multiply l_i by λ_i' in Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates is obvious but depends on the pants decomposition;
- he proposes a geometric retraction: cap each boundary circle with the cone (disc) on it, conformally determined by the hyperbolic arclength.

The 'specific problem on hyperbolic pants' to be put to Bers comes later in the letter.
errors: The rigidification is stated as 'a homotopy equivalence between X_0 and X∖S'. Strictly one needs the class of an orientation-preserving homeomorphism (equivalently a homotopy equivalence respecting orientation and peripheral structure, up to isotopy). A bare homotopy equivalence is too weak and ambiguous. This is a minor imprecision of formulation.
'with a system of points' is missing the symbol ν, a typing omission. 'introducing' should read 'introduced'. These are cosmetic.

ideas.what: Teichmüller space of genus g curves with ν marked points as universal cover of the moduli stack, homeomorphic to C^{3g-3+ν}
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space T_{g,n} as orbifold universal cover of M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Teichmüller, Ahlfors, Bers; stack viewpoint Deligne–Mumford
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower; Cartan seminar 1960-61 exposés on Teichmüller space

ideas.what: Teichmüller space of compact bordered Riemann surfaces, ≅ C^d × (R_{>0})^ν, with boundary geodesic lengths as extra parameters
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space of hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary / bordered Teichmüller space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fenchel–Nielsen, Thurston; Abikoff, Bers for bordered surfaces

ideas.what: Partial compactification allowing boundary lengths to be 0 (boundary components degenerate to punctures), a manifold with corners containing T_{g,ν} as boundary stratum
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space with boundary lengths in R_{≥0}^n; the family T_{g,n}(L) with L→0 giving cusps
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in Thurston school; systematically used by Mirzakhani (2007), Mondello, Do–Norbury
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse's 'chirurgie' of surfaces; not explicitly

ideas.what: Request for an intrinsic (pants-decomposition-free) Mod-equivariant action of (R_{≥0})^ν rescaling boundary lengths, giving a retraction of bordered Teichmüller space onto punctured Teichmüller space
ideas.modern_name: Canonical trivialization T(L) ≅ T(0) × fibre; comparison of Teichmüller spaces with different boundary lengths
ideas.usually_credited_to: No canonical such action is standard; non-canonical diffeomorphisms T(L)≅T(L') are folklore

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for an intrinsic, mapping-class-group-equivariant semigroup action of (R_{≥0})^ν on the partially compactified bordered Teichmüller space. Its quotient/retraction would identify punctured Teichmüller space, and the action should be independent of pants decompositions. Literature mostly uses non-canonical identifications T(L)≅T(0), or the L→∞ ribbon-graph limit. A canonical rescaling action of this form does not appear to be a standard object.
missed.quote: Our interest is in pinpointing the precise relationship between the two modular spaces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mirzakhani-type volume recursion and Kontsevich/Penner ribbon-graph models interpolate between L=0 and L→∞. An intrinsic equivariant trivialization of the boundary-length family, e.g. via capping by discs as he proposes next, would give a canonical bridge. It may connect to Mondello's and Do's work on the length-deformation of moduli spaces.

missed.claim: This is the existence and content of a 1984 letter from Grothendieck to Lipman Bers on Thurston's approach to Teichmüller theory, from the Grothendieck–Ladegaillerie microseminar, contemporaneous with Esquisse d'un programme. It documents the analytic/hyperbolic side of his 'surgery of surfaces' programme and appears little known.
missed.quote: as I understand you are the main expert on Thurston's hyperbolic geometry approach to Teichmüller space
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence of how the Teichmüller tower and Esquisse were connected to hyperbolic geometry and pants decompositions, and of contacts with the Bers school.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is standard: T_{g,n}, bordered Teichmüller space, and the L→0 limit to cusps. The interest is historical: an apparently little-known letter to Bers. There is also a mildly original request for an intrinsic rescaling action/retraction, whose substance is developed on the following pages.
